features.name: Brand email-OTP signup/verify/register/login
features.user_type: Brand (unauthenticated visitor becoming a Brand user)
features.purpose: Prove ownership of an email before/independent of registration, then create a Brand user + Workspace + Wallet + Free subscription, or authenticate an existing Brand user.
features.flow: FE src/pages/brand-register.tsx / brand-login.tsx -> src/lib/api.ts -> AuthController (send/verify/register/login) -> BrandEmailOtpService.sendOtp/verifyOtp (EmailOtpChallenge row, Msg91EmailClient) for OTP; AuthService.brandRegister/brandLogin (AuthService.java:125-301) for account creation/auth -> UserRepository/WorkspaceRepository/WorkspaceMemberRepository/WalletRepository/SubscriptionService -> AuthCookieService writes HttpOnly refresh cookie -> ApiResponse<TokenPair> (refresh stripped) to FE.
features.api: POST /auth/brand/send-email-otp (permitAll), POST /auth/brand/verify-email (permitAll), POST /auth/brand/register (auth via POST /auth/** permitAll), POST /auth/brand/login (same). All under context-path /api/v1.
features.database: users (INSERT, UNIQUE email+phone), workspaces (INSERT), workspace_members (INSERT owner row), wallets (INSERT), subscriptions (INSERT free tier via SubscriptionService.getOrCreateFreeSubscription), email_otp_challenges (INSERT/UPDATE), refresh_tokens (INSERT).
features.state_machine: User.status: PENDING_VERIFICATION on create -> ACTIVE once isEmailVerified is set true (either at register time if requireEmailOtpBeforeRegister, or later via reset-password/login-time OTP recovery). EmailOtpChallenge: issued -> verified (consumed) -> optionally required-and-consumed at register.
features.authn: send/verify OTP endpoints are permitAll (unauthenticated by design, pre-account). register/login are POST /auth/** permitAll matchers (SecurityConfig.java:87-88).
features.authz: None beyond email-ownership proof; register enforces phone/email uniqueness and PasswordPolicy server-side (AuthService.java:127-163).
features.working_condition: A previously-unregistered email can send+verify an OTP (if requireEmailOtpBeforeRegister is on) or skip straight to register (default off), get a 201 with a stripped TokenPair plus an HttpOnly refresh cookie, and subsequently log in with the same credentials, landing in the newly created workspace.
features.failure_conditions: Duplicate email/phone -> 409 EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS/PHONE_ALREADY_EXISTS (upfront check + DataIntegrityViolationException catch for the TOCTOU race, AuthService.java:127-163,193-221). Weak password -> PasswordPolicy exception. Missing/malformed phone -> 400 PHONE_REQUIRED / validation error. Wrong password on login -> 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS. Suspended/deactivated user.status -> 403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED (see known issue below: this status is never actually written by product code). Unverified + requireEmailVerification -> 403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED.
features.security_conditions: Password BCrypt strength 12 (SecurityConfig.java:~303). OTP send is rate-limited by AuthRateLimitFilter (per-IP) plus a DB-backed per-IP (8/hr) and per-email-global (10/hr) cap in BrandEmailOtpService.java:60-74, distinct layers. getRemoteAddr() (not raw X-Forwarded-For) is used deliberately per AuthController.java:54-57 comment to prevent IP-cap bypass via a spoofed header. Refresh token never exposed to JS (HttpOnly cookie via AuthCookieService).
features.tests: AuthServiceTest (64 tests, all pass) covers AuthService.brandRegister/brandLogin logic directly (service layer). AuthControllerTest.java has ZERO tests exercising brandRegister/brandLogin/sendBrandEmailOtp/verifyBrandEmail controller methods -- every listed @Test in that file is creator-scoped (sendCreatorEmailOtp_delegates, creatorRegister_writesCookieAndStripsRefresh, creatorLogin_writesCookieAndStripsRefresh, etc.). The brand controller methods are structurally identical to the tested creator ones (same cookie-writing call), which lowers but does not eliminate the risk of an untested divergence.
features.production_conditions: influora.auth.require-email-otp-before-register (default false) and influora.auth.require-email-verification (default true) must be set consistently, or a signup can be bricked at 2nd login per the F-0601 history described in BrandEmailOtpService.java:118-128 (this RC's sendOtp already covers the 'unverified but already registered' recovery case). influora.web-base-url must be set for reset-password links (used elsewhere, not this flow directly).
features.evidence: AuthController.java:51-89 (controller wiring); AuthService.java:125-301 (brandRegister/brandLogin bodies, read in full); BrandEmailOtpService.java:1-140 (OTP issuance/caps, read in full); AuthServiceTest surefire report: Tests run 64, Failures 0, Errors 0; AuthControllerTest.java grep shows only creator-scoped @Test methods, no brand ones.

features.name: Token refresh + logout
features.purpose: Rotate a long-lived refresh token for a new short-lived access token without re-entering credentials, and terminate a session on logout.
features.flow: FE fetchWithAuthRetry (src/lib/api.ts) -> POST /auth/refresh (cookie-first, JSON-body fallback) -> AuthService.refresh (AuthService.java:534-641): validates token hash+expiry+revoked, re-checks account/workspace/creator-profile suspension state (AUTH-1/F-0451/F-0458 gates), revokes the presented token, mints+persists a new one, re-derives workspaceId via the same deterministic ordering as login -> AuthCookieService rewrites the cookie -> RefreshResponse{access, expiresIn}. Logout -> AuthService.logout revokes ALL refresh tokens for the user, controller clears the cookie unconditionally.
features.api: POST /auth/refresh (permitAll, since no access token exists at call time by design), POST /auth/logout (authenticated, but code tolerates principal==null and still clears the cookie).
features.database: refresh_tokens: SELECT by token_hash+revoked=false+expires_at>now, UPDATE revoked=true (old row), INSERT new row. logout: bulk UPDATE revokeAllForUser.
features.state_machine: RefreshToken: active -> revoked (single-use rotation, Kabir B3). remembered flag is carried forward from the presented token, never re-derived (AuthService.java:622-626), so a refresh cannot silently upgrade/downgrade session length.
features.authn: refresh reads the HttpOnly cookie via AuthCookieService.readRefreshToken, falling back to a request-body token only if the cookie is absent (AuthController.java:136-143). logout requires @AuthenticationPrincipal but null-checks it rather than 401ing.
features.authz: None beyond token possession; refresh independently re-checks SUSPENDED/DEACTIVATED user status, EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED, and workspace/creator-profile suspension every single rotation (AuthService.java:569-616) -- this closes the gap noted in the AUTH-1/F-0451 comments where a 30-day refresh window could otherwise outlive a login-time-only suspension check.
features.working_condition: A valid, unrevoked, unexpired refresh token (cookie or body) yields a new access token and a rotated refresh cookie; the account/workspace suspension gates are re-evaluated on every call, not just at login.
features.failure_conditions: Missing token (cookie AND body) -> 401 INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN (AuthController.java:140-143). Revoked/expired/unknown hash -> 401 INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN, and the presented token is NOT burned in that case (guards run before the revoke/rotate block, AuthService.java:556-568 comment). Suspended user/workspace/creator-profile -> 403 (ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED/WORKSPACE_SUSPENDED), again without burning the token.
features.security_conditions: Kabir B3 single-use rotation. Kabir A1: refresh token never reaches JS, only the cookie. The fallback JSON body path (AuthController.java:126-129 comment) is a 'transitional' allowance for non-browser clients with no environment gate -- it is always available in this RC, not dev-only.
features.tests: AuthControllerTest: refresh_missingToken, refresh_cookieHappyPath, refresh_bodyFallback, logout_clearsCookie all present and (per file inspection) exercise the controller directly. AuthServiceTest's 64 tests (all passing) include the AuthService.refresh/logout logic per the class's scope, though this session did not enumerate which of the 64 map to refresh specifically.
features.production_conditions: JwtService's access/refresh expiry configuration and AuthCookieService's cookie flags (HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite) must be correctly set per environment; not independently re-verified in this pass beyond reading AuthCookieService.java's structure.
features.evidence: AuthController.java:125-161 (read in full); AuthService.java:520-646 (RefreshRotation record + refresh + logout, read in full); AuthControllerTest.java grep showing refresh_missingToken/refresh_cookieHappyPath/refresh_bodyFallback/logout_clearsCookie test names.
known_issues: The JSON-body refresh-token fallback (AuthController.java:133,137-139) has no environment restriction; it exists permanently as an alternate path alongside the cookie, which is a broader attack surface than a cookie-only design (mitigated by the fact that an attacker still needs the raw refresh token value itself).
No scheduled job purges revoked/expired refresh_tokens rows -- see the Jobs feature entry; this table only grows.

features.name: Forgot/reset password
features.user_type: Brand and Creator (shared code path, role-agnostic reset page)
features.purpose: Let a user who forgot their password request a mailed reset link and set a new password from it.
features.entry_point: POST /auth/forgot-password, POST /auth/reset-password (AuthController.java:163,170); FE routes /brand/forgot-password, /creator/forgot-password both funnel into the same /reset-password page (App.tsx:215-220, role-agnostic per that comment)
features.flow: FE brand-forgot-password.tsx / creator-forgot-password.tsx -> POST /auth/forgot-password -> AuthService.forgotPassword (AuthService.java:662-666): looks up by email, silently no-ops if not found, else createPasswordResetToken -> PasswordResetTokenRepository.save + PasswordResetEvent published (email dispatch, out of this domain) -> generic 'If this email exists...' response always. FE /reset-password?token=... -> BrandResetPasswordPage -> POST /auth/reset-password -> AuthService.resetPassword (AuthService.java:668-772): validates token hash+unused+unexpired, rejects a soft-deleted or SUSPENDED/DEACTIVATED user, sets new password hash, marks email verified, revokes ALL refresh tokens.
features.database: password_reset_tokens (INSERT on forgot, SELECT+UPDATE used=true on reset), users (UPDATE password_hash, email_verified), refresh_tokens (bulk revoke on successful reset).
features.state_machine: PasswordResetToken: issued -> used (single-use) or expires after 3600s (AuthService.java:868, TTL literal). A successful reset also promotes User.status PENDING_VERIFICATION -> ACTIVE via setEmailVerified(true) (AuthService.java:762-766), which is the only self-service recovery path for accounts stranded by the F-0601 verification-email-never-sent incident referenced in project memory.
features.authn: None (this is the pre-authentication recovery path by design).
features.authz: None; identity is proven purely by possession of the mailed token.
features.working_condition: forgot-password always returns the same generic message regardless of whether the email exists (anti-enumeration); reset-password with a valid unexpired unused token for a non-deleted, non-suspended user rotates the password hash, marks email verified, and revokes every outstanding session.
features.failure_conditions: Invalid/expired/used token -> 400 INVALID_RESET_TOKEN. Soft-deleted user (deletedAt != null) -> same 400 INVALID_RESET_TOKEN, deliberately not a distinct code per AuthService.java:701-721's reasoning (already proven mailbox ownership means no enumeration risk). SUSPENDED/DEACTIVATED user.status -> 403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED (AuthService.java:746-748) -- but see known issue below: this check does NOT look at Workspace.isSuspended()/CreatorProfile.isSuspended(), which are the flags product suspension actually writes.
features.security_conditions: Reset link embeds the raw token in a mailto link built from influora.web-base-url (AuthService.java:881); in dev profile the raw token is ALSO logged (AuthService.java:869-874) -- confirmed gated on environment.isDev(), not always-on. Token hash stored, not raw value (JwtService.hashToken). AccountController's DELETE /me/account path calls purgePasswordResetTokens to close the window where a link mailed before deletion could still write a fresh password onto an anonymized row (AuthService.java:690-721 documents this was previously exploitable up to 7 days for the sponsor-provisioning variant).
features.tests: No forgotPassword/resetPassword controller-level test found in AuthControllerTest.java (grep for 'forgotPassword|resetPassword' against that file returned nothing). AuthServiceTest's 64 tests are the only direct exercise of this logic found in this pass; not individually itemized here.
features.production_conditions: influora.web-base-url must be set (used to build the reset link) and PasswordResetEvent's listener/mailer must actually be wired for non-dev profiles to deliver the email at all (out of this domain's direct file scope to re-verify the mailer wiring).
features.evidence: AuthController.java:163-175 (controller, read in full); AuthService.java:662-772,846-884 (forgotPassword/resetPassword/createPasswordResetToken, read in full); App.tsx grep showing /reset-password -> BrandResetPasswordPage with an explicit role-agnostic comment.
known_issues: resetPassword's suspension guard (AuthService.java:746-748) checks users.status (SUSPENDED/DEACTIVATED), which per the code's own comment (AuthService.java:732-740) is NEVER written by any src/main code path -- actual product suspension lives on Workspace.isSuspended() (brand) and CreatorProfile.isSuspended() (creator), neither of which resetPassword consults. A workspace-suspended brand or profile-suspended creator can therefore still successfully complete a password reset (proving mailbox control) even though they still cannot log in afterward, because the login paths DO check those flags independently. Same gap exists in changePassword (AuthService.java:813-822, self-documented as open there too).
No forgotPassword/resetPassword test exists at the AuthController (web) layer.
required_fixes: If the intent is that a suspended brand/creator cannot rotate credentials at all (not just cannot log in with them), add Workspace/CreatorProfile suspension checks to resetPassword and changePassword, matching the checks already present in brandLogin/creatorLogin/refresh.

features.name: Account self-service: DELETE /me/account, POST /me/password, GET/PATCH /users/me
features.purpose: Let a logged-in user soft-delete their own account, change their password in-session, and read/update their own profile fields.
features.flow: DELETE /me/account -> AccountController.deleteAccount -> UserRepository.findById -> User.softDelete() (anonymizes PII, stamps deletedAt) -> save -> AuthService.logout (revoke all refresh tokens) -> AuthService.purgePasswordResetTokens -> AuthCookieService.clearRefreshCookie. POST /me/password -> AccountController.changePassword reads the caller's own raw refresh cookie -> AuthService.changePassword (verify currentPassword, F-0703 suspension check, set new hash, revoke all OTHER refresh tokens excluding the caller's own live one). GET/PATCH /users/me -> UserController -> UserService.getProfile/updateProfile -> UserRepository (partial-update semantics: only non-null fields in UpdateProfileRequest are applied, UserService.java:45-51).
features.api: DELETE /me/account, POST /me/password, GET /users/me, PATCH /users/me -- all under the default anyRequest().authenticated() rule (SecurityConfig.java:~298), no permitAll.
features.database: users: UPDATE (soft-delete fields, password_hash, profile fields). refresh_tokens: bulk revoke (all, or all-except-current). password_reset_tokens: DELETE by userId on account deletion.
features.state_machine: User: active -> soft-deleted (deletedAt set, PII nulled, id/status/userType preserved for FK integrity per AccountController.java:29-33 javadoc). Deletion deliberately does NOT cascade into deals/contracts/messages/workspaces.
features.authn: @AuthenticationPrincipal AuthPrincipal required on all four endpoints (no null-tolerant paths here, unlike /auth/logout).
features.authz: Self-only by construction: every operation is scoped to principal.getUserId(), no target-id parameter exists on any of these endpoints.
features.working_condition: An authenticated user can delete their own account (immediately losing all sessions), change their password (keeping their own current session alive per the e60d249 fix), and read/patch their own first/last/display name via PATCH (no password field accepted there, per UserDtos.UpdateProfileRequest having no password property -- confirmed by grep).
features.failure_conditions: deleteAccount: USER_NOT_FOUND 404 if the row is somehow already gone. changePassword: wrong currentPassword -> 401 INVALID_CURRENT_PASSWORD; SUSPENDED/DEACTIVATED users.status -> 403 (same never-written-in-product-code caveat as resetPassword); weak newPassword -> PasswordPolicy exception.
features.security_conditions: [SEC: Kabir H-1 -- PARTIAL, creators only per AccountController.java:35-52 javadoc] Deleting an account revokes refresh tokens but does NOT invalidate an already-issued access token (stateless JWT, no DB round-trip) -- immediate effect relies on per-request context gates re-checking deletedAt. The javadoc states BrandContextService.requireBrand now performs this check as of F-0708 (2026-09-07), closing a gap where a soft-deleted BRAND user kept full brand-scoped access (including wallet/payout endpoints) until token expiry; CreatorContextService.requireCreator always checked it. This was NOT independently re-verified in this pass by opening BrandContextService.java -- flagged as a verification gap, not a confirmed-open bug, since the comment is dated and specific (references a named test and gate script).
features.tests: AccountControllerTest.java has exactly 2 tests, both scoped to DELETE /me/account's ordering guarantees (testDeleteAccountPurgesPasswordResetTokens, testDeleteAccountSavesBeforePurging) -- POST /me/password has NO AccountController-level test. UserController.java has NO dedicated test file at all (confirmed: no UserControllerTest.java under src/test); UserServiceTest.java (22 tests) covers the service layer underneath GET/PATCH /users/me but not the controller/HTTP wiring. AuthRateLimitFilterMePasswordBucketTest.java exists and presumably covers the rate-limit bucket for POST /me/password specifically (not opened in this pass).
features.production_conditions: Depends on BrandContextService/CreatorContextService actually being wired into every brand/creator-scoped controller for the deletedAt check to have the claimed immediate effect -- this pass verified the claim only via AccountController's javadoc, not by opening BrandContextService.java itself.
features.evidence: AccountController.java:1-136 (read in full); UserController.java:1-39 (read in full); UserService.java:24-51 (getProfile/updateProfile, partial read); UserDtos.java grep showing no password field on UpdateProfileRequest; AccountControllerTest.java and JwksControllerTest.java @Test method listings; confirmed absence of any UserControllerTest*.java file via find.
known_issues: No AccountController-level test for POST /me/password (change-password), only for DELETE /me/account.
No UserController-level test at all; GET/PATCH /users/me correctness is inferred from UserServiceTest, not proven at the HTTP/controller layer.
changePassword shares resetPassword's Workspace/CreatorProfile suspension-check gap (see Forgot/reset password entry) -- self-documented as open at AuthService.java:813-822.

The claim that BrandContextService now re-checks deletedAt (closing the brand-side of Kabir H-1) was read from a code comment in AccountController, not independently confirmed by opening BrandContextService.java in this pass.
required_fixes: Add an AccountControllerTest case for POST /me/password (happy path + wrong-current-password + own-session-preserved assertion).
Add a UserControllerTest for GET/PATCH /users/me at the web layer.

features.name: Admin login/refresh/logout/me + TOTP MFA setup/verify
features.purpose: Third, fully separate auth realm for the admin panel: password+optional-TOTP login with failed-attempt lockout, its own refresh-token rotation, and self-service MFA enrollment.
features.entry_point: POST /admin/auth/login, /refresh, /logout, GET /admin/auth/me, POST /admin/auth/mfa/setup, /mfa/verify (AdminAuthController.java:69-126); FE /admin/login -> admin-login.tsx, session lifecycle in src/admin/services/admin-session.ts
features.flow: FE admin-login.tsx -> src/admin/services/api-contracts.ts authApi.login -> apiRequest('/auth/login') against ADMIN_API_BASE='/api/v1/admin' -> AdminAuthController.login -> AdminAuthService.login (AdminAuthService.java:107-175): password check, lockout check (admin.isLockedOut), MFA-required-if-enabled check with its own lockout counter, MFA-enforce-on-login policy for SUPER_ADMIN/ADMIN roles (AdminSecurityProperties.isMfaEnforceOnLogin, default true) -> issueTokens -> AdminAuthCookieService writes a path-scoped (/api/v1/admin/auth) SameSite=Strict refresh cookie -> raw LoginResponse (NOT ApiResponse-wrapped, deliberate deviation documented in AdminAuthController.java:35-47). Refresh/logout/me/mfa/* mirror the brand/creator shapes but write to admin_users/admin_refresh_tokens.
features.api: POST /admin/auth/login, /admin/auth/refresh permitAll (SecurityConfig.java:263-266); everything else under /admin/** requires hasRole('ADMIN') (SecurityConfig.java:276-277).
features.database: admin_users (SELECT/UPDATE failed_login_attempts, failed_mfa_attempts, last_login_at, encrypted_mfa_secret, mfa_enabled), admin_refresh_tokens (INSERT/UPDATE revoke+rotate).
features.state_machine: AdminUser MFA: not-enrolled -> staged (setupMfa writes encrypted_mfa_secret but mfa_enabled stays false) -> enabled (verifyMfa confirms a working code, AdminUser.confirmMfa). Lockout: normal -> locked (failed_login_attempts >= AdminSecurityProperties.lockoutMaxAttempts) -> unlocked after lockoutCooldownSeconds. Separate MFA-code lockout counter (tighter: 3 attempts/1hr vs 5/15min for password).
features.authn: login/refresh permitAll; logout/me/mfa/* require an already-issued ROLE_ADMIN JWT (AuthPrincipal), resolved via AdminContextService.requireAdminId inside the service, not at the controller.
features.authz: roleRequiresMfa() gates SUPER_ADMIN/ADMIN into mandatory MFA-at-login (SUPPORT exempt) -- code comment flags this MUST stay in lockstep with AdminContextService#requireMfaSatisfied's identical split, a manually-maintained invariant with no shared constant or test cross-checking the two.
features.working_condition: A correct password (+ correct TOTP code if mfa_enabled, or outright login-refusal via MFA_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED if the role requires MFA but it is unenrolled) issues an access+refresh token pair; /me returns the caller's own AdminUserDto; MFA setup/verify enroll a new TOTP secret two-step (stage then confirm).
features.failure_conditions: Bad password/unknown email -> generic 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS (enumeration-safe, Kabir P1-2 Gap 3). Locked out (either counter) -> same generic 401, no distinguishing signal. Inactive admin -> 403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED. MFA required but code missing -> 401 MFA_REQUIRED. Wrong MFA code -> generic 401 (never a distinct 'wrong code' message, to avoid timing/enumeration leakage per the code comment). features.name: Admin MFA reset POST /admin/auth/mfa/reset/{id}
features.user_type: Admin (SUPER_ADMIN only, acting on a different admin)
features.purpose: Recovery path for a SUPER_ADMIN or ADMIN locked out of their own MFA device, without a direct DB edit.
features.flow: Caller (must already hold a ROLE_ADMIN JWT with MFA satisfied) -> AdminAuthController.resetMfaForAdmin -> AdminAuthService.resetMfaForAdmin (AdminAuthService.java:341-354): AdminContextService.requireRoleWithMfaSatisfied(principal, SUPER_ADMIN) re-derives the caller's own id server-side (never trusts the path/body), rejects self-targeting, loads the target via loadActive, clears their MFA enrollment (AdminUser.resetMfa()), and bulk-revokes every admin_refresh_tokens row for the TARGET.
features.api: POST /admin/auth/mfa/reset/{targetAdminId}, under the blanket /admin/** hasRole('ADMIN') matcher (no more specific SUPER_ADMIN-at-the-filter-level matcher exists -- enforcement is entirely inside AdminContextService.requireRoleWithMfaSatisfied).
features.database: admin_users: UPDATE (clear encrypted_mfa_secret/mfa_enabled on target). admin_refresh_tokens: bulk revoke for target.
features.state_machine: Target AdminUser: mfa_enabled=true -> mfa_enabled=false (forced back through setup+verify on next login/privileged action).
features.authz: Enforced entirely in the service, not the controller/filter: caller must be an ACTIVE SUPER_ADMIN with their OWN MFA already satisfied (AdminContextService.requireRoleWithMfaSatisfied), and may not target their own adminId (checked against the caller id re-derived server-side, never from the path param, per AdminAuthService.java:320-324 comment). Target must be an active admin row.
features.working_condition: An active, MFA-satisfied SUPER_ADMIN can clear a DIFFERENT active admin's MFA enrollment and immediately kill that target's outstanding sessions, forcing re-enrollment.
features.failure_conditions: Non-SUPER_ADMIN caller -> rejected by AdminContextService before any row is touched (test: nonSuperAdminCallerIsRejected). Self-targeting -> 403 CANNOT_RESET_OWN_MFA (test: selfResetIsRejected). Inactive/nonexistent target -> ADMIN_NOT_FOUND via loadActive.
features.security_conditions: F-0648 fix (documented in AdminAuthService.java:332-339): clearing mfa_enabled alone used to leave the target's existing refresh tokens valid until natural expiry, defeating the point of a compromised-session recovery path; now every target role (including SUPPORT, which is exempt from the MFA gate itself) has its sessions revoked as part of the reset.
features.tests: AdminAuthServiceTest.java's entire 5-test suite is dedicated to this one method (authorizedSuperAdminResetsAnotherAdminsMfa, resetMfaRevokesTargetsRefreshTokens_superAdminTarget, resetMfaRevokesTargetsRefreshTokens_supportTarget, nonSuperAdminCallerIsRejected, selfResetIsRejected) -- confirmed passing (5/5) by running the suite in this pass. This is the best-tested piece of the admin auth surface.
features.production_conditions: No FE caller exists for this endpoint (per the task's own pointer and not contradicted by anything found in src/admin in this pass) -- recovery today would have to be performed via a direct API call (curl/Postman) by an operator, not through the admin SPA.
features.evidence: AdminAuthController.java:128-141 (read in full); AdminAuthService.java:308-354 (read in full); AdminAuthServiceTest.java @Test listing (5 methods) plus surefire run: Tests run 5, Failures 0, Errors 0.
known_issues: No frontend UI calls this endpoint -- confirmed absent from the api-contracts.ts grep output captured in this pass (no '/auth/mfa/reset' reference seen); a locked-out admin's recovery today depends on another operator making a raw API call, not on any admin-panel button.
required_fixes: Either add an admin-panel UI action for a SUPER_ADMIN to trigger this (e.g. from an admin-user detail screen) or explicitly document that this is an ops-only, curl-driven recovery path.

features.name: JWKS GET /.well-known/jwks.json, GET /config/public, GET /health
features.user_type: Unauthenticated (all three) -- JWKS consumed by influora-ai's PyJWKClient, /config/public by pre-signup SPA pages, /health by uptime monitoring
features.purpose: Publish the public signing key set for cross-service JWT verification; expose non-secret client config before any account exists; report liveness including a real DB check.
features.flow: JWKS: influora-ai PyJWKClient -> GET /.well-known/jwks.json -> JwksController.jwks() -> SpringJwksKeyService.publicJwkSet() -> each Jwk<?> (a Map) copied into a plain LinkedHashMap (toPlainMap) specifically to avoid a documented Jackson serialization crash on jjwt's concrete Jwk type -> {"keys": [...]}. Public config: SPA pre-signup pages -> GET /config/public -> PublicConfigResponse{requireEmailOtp} mirroring AuthService's own @Value flag. Health: uptime checks -> GET /health -> Spring Actuator HealthEndpoint (auto-wires DataSourceHealthIndicator, real DB ping) + R2StorageService.isAvailable() -> {status, storage.r2}.
features.database: None directly for JWKS/config; /health indirectly pings the datasource via the actuator HealthIndicator (no explicit query written by HealthController itself).
features.authn: None -- all permitAll by design, each with an explicit justification comment (JWKS: public key material only, safe by RFC 7517 convention; config: pre-account pages need it; health: infra monitoring).
features.working_condition: JWKS returns exactly the public key(s) with a kid, serializable without the documented Jackson/jjwt RedactedSupplier crash; /config/public's requireEmailOtp flag matches AuthService's own enforcement; /health returns DOWN (not silently 'ok') when the DB is unreachable.
features.failure_conditions: None modeled beyond infra failure (DB down -> /health reports DOWN via actuator).
features.security_conditions: JwksController explicitly has no access to the private key (only depends on the key service, which never exposes it through a JSON-serializable method, per the class javadoc). PublicConfigController's javadoc explicitly warns that Razorpay's keySecret must NEVER be added to this controller's /public branch -- correctly, getRazorpayConfig() only returns keyId and is a SEPARATE, non-permitAll endpoint.
features.tests: JwksControllerTest.java: 2 tests (testJwksReturnsExpectedShape, testJwksNeverExposesPrivateKeyMaterial), both passing (2/2, confirmed by running the suite). SpringJwksKeyServiceTest.java also exists (not opened in this pass). No PublicConfigControllerTest or HealthControllerTest found by this pass's file listing.

features.name: Jobs: StaleTokenCleanupJob, IdempotencyReservationReaperJob
features.purpose: Background hygiene sweeps named in this domain's task list, but on inspection neither one actually operates on brand/creator/admin auth tables.
features.flow: StaleTokenCleanupJob queries MetaOAuthTokenRepository.findByExpiresAtBeforeAndRevokedFalse(now - 14 days) and calls MetaOAuthToken.revoke()+save per stale row, then writes an AuditLogService.recordToolCall summary -- this operates ENTIRELY on Meta/Instagram OAuth connection tokens (creator social-account linkage), NOT on this domain's refresh_tokens/admin_refresh_tokens. IdempotencyReservationReaperJob queries IdempotencyKeyRecordRepository for IN_PROGRESS rows older than 15 minutes and atomically flips them to FAILED via a conditional UPDATE (reclaimStaleInProgress), handing them back to IdempotencyService's own reclaimFailedForRetry path -- this is a generic cross-domain safety net (payouts, campaign actions, etc. that use IdempotencyService.executeOnce), not specific to authentication either.
features.database: StaleTokenCleanupJob: meta_oauth_tokens (UPDATE revoked=true). IdempotencyReservationReaperJob: idempotency_key_records (conditional UPDATE status IN_PROGRESS->FAILED).
features.state_machine: MetaOAuthToken: active -> revoked (soft-revoke only, never deleted, per the class's stated pattern). IdempotencyKeyRecord: IN_PROGRESS -> FAILED (abandoned-reservation reclaim) -> (next legitimate call) retryable.
features.working_condition: Both jobs run on their cron schedule, take a ShedLock to prevent double-execution across instances, single-flight-guard against re-entrancy within one instance (AtomicBoolean running), and per-row try/catch so one bad row never aborts the batch.
features.failure_conditions: A per-row exception is caught, logged, and counted as failed/skipped without aborting the rest of the sweep (both jobs share this pattern explicitly).
features.security_conditions: Neither job writes to refresh_tokens or admin_refresh_tokens (confirmed by grep: no reference to RefreshTokenRepository/AdminRefreshTokenRepository anywhere under src/main/java/com/influora/job/). Consequently: revoked/expired rows in refresh_tokens and admin_refresh_tokens are NEVER purged by any job found in this codebase -- those tables grow without bound as every login/register/refresh/admin-login/admin-refresh call inserts a new row and rotation/logout only ever sets revoked=true, never deletes.
features.tests: No test files found for either job under src/test in this pass's search (search targeted the job names specifically and returned only the src/main files).
features.production_conditions: Requires shedlock's distributed-lock table to be present and correctly migrated for multi-instance deployments; not independently re-verified in this pass.
features.evidence: StaleTokenCleanupJob.java (read in full); IdempotencyReservationReaperJob.java (read in full); grep across src/main/java/com/influora/job/ and the two repositories for RefreshTokenRepository/AdminRefreshTokenRepository returned zero hits.
known_issues: Neither job in this domain's task list actually touches this domain's own tables (refresh_tokens, admin_refresh_tokens, password_reset_tokens, email_otp_challenges) -- StaleTokenCleanupJob is scoped to Meta OAuth tokens and IdempotencyReservationReaperJob is a generic cross-cutting concern. This looks like a domain-assignment mismatch in the audit task list rather than a defect in the jobs themselves.

No scheduled job purges revoked or expired rows from refresh_tokens, admin_refresh_tokens, password_reset_tokens, or email_otp_challenges anywhere in this codebase (confirmed by the negative grep above) -- these tables grow unboundedly forever. Low severity (storage cost only, no functional or security impact since revoked/expired rows are already unusable), but worth a cleanup job of the same shape as StaleTokenCleanupJob.
required_fixes: Add a scheduled job (same ShedLock+AtomicBoolean+per-row-try/catch pattern already established) to hard-delete or archive refresh_tokens/admin_refresh_tokens/password_reset_tokens/email_otp_challenges rows that are revoked/used/expired past a retention window.
Correct the audit task list's domain assignment for these two jobs, or explicitly scope this domain's 'Jobs' entry to note that no auth-table-specific cleanup job currently exists.

findings.title: resetPassword and changePassword do not check Workspace/CreatorProfile suspension, only the never-written users.status enum
findings.evidence: AuthService.java:669-772 (resetPassword) and :795-844 (changePassword) both check only `user.getStatus() == UserStatus.SUSPENDED || DEACTIVATED`. AuthService.java:732-740's own comment states plainly that nothing in src/main ever writes UserStatus.SUSPENDED/DEACTIVATED -- product suspension is Workspace.isSuspended() (brand) or CreatorProfile.isSuspended() (creator), which brandLogin/creatorLogin/refresh DO check (AuthService.java:295,338-360,503-512,594-616) but resetPassword/changePassword do not.
findings.impact: A brand whose workspace has been suspended by an admin, or a creator whose profile has been suspended, can still successfully complete a password reset or an in-session password change (proving/reusing credential control) even though they cannot subsequently log in with the new password, since the login paths independently re-check workspace/profile suspension. Limited real-world impact (no access is actually granted), but it is a genuine, code-confirmed inconsistency between what login blocks and what credential-rotation blocks.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend resetPassword and changePassword to also reject when the user's active workspace is suspended (brand) or their CreatorProfile.isSuspended() is true (creator), mirroring the checks already present in brandLogin/creatorLogin/refresh.
findings.reproduction: As an admin, suspend a brand's workspace (or a creator's profile) via the existing admin suspend endpoint; as that user, call POST /auth/forgot-password then POST /auth/reset-password with the mailed token -- the reset succeeds despite the account being suspended.
findings.verification_required: A live/integration test suspending a workspace or creator profile and then calling resetPassword/changePassword to confirm it is NOT rejected, to move this from OBSERVED (code-read) to VERIFIED (runtime-reproduced).
